statement: The input is a Python 3 function that is meant to return the sum over i of xs[i] * ys[i], taken modulo m (xs and ys have the same length, m is positive). It contains exactly one bug: an off-by-one, a wrong operator, or a wrong initial value. Fix the bug, then evaluate the corrected function for the call `dot_mod([35, 3, 15, 29, 36, 6, 7, 10], [28, 20, 1, 12, 24, 4, 25, 3], 290)`. Answer with the integer it returns.
title: Blue belt: fix dot_mod
